title: Texoma HIDTA Executive Board employment recommendations

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Texas Public Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. All records reflecting, transmitting or documenting the Texoma HIDTA Executive Board's vote or recommendation to terminate Rick Milteer's employment, as referenced in the letter of December 28, 2020 from Human Resources Coordinator Julie Wright. This includes the letter itself, any minutes, notes or recordings of the Board meeting at which the vote was taken, and any communication conveying the vote or recommendation to the County.
2. All records, from January 1, 2025 through the date of this request, reflecting any vote, recommendation, approval, direction or request by the Texoma HIDTA Executive Board, or by any of its members or committees, about hiring, terminating, disciplining, promoting, reclassifying or setting the pay of any person employed by the County in a position funded by a HIDTA grant or assigned to the Texoma HIDTA.

For both items, "records" includes records held by County officers and employees assigned to the Texoma HIDTA, including the Director's office, whether kept on County systems or on other systems used for that work.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

HCvP

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: Signal messages – Aleks Wolan (legislative aide)
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

I ask that you acknowledge receipt of this record request once received, and ask for a determination before or on November 30, 2026, per the CPRA, and an even faster reply if you can make that determination without reviewing the record(s) in question.

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act ("CPRA") [Gov't Code §§ 7920.000 et seq.] and the California Constitution [Cal. Const., art. I, § 3(b)(1)], I therefore request the following records in the "possession, control of, relating to, to be about, or to bear on" the City of Berkeley.

RECORDS REQUESTED:

1. Message Threads (Chat History)

All message threads contained on the “Signal” application on the City-issued mobile devices and personal devices of Aleks Wolan, including all messages sent and received, as retained on the application as of November 20, 2026. This includes, for each thread, the complete conversation history from its beginning through the date of this request, with all preceding and subsequent messages preserved in context.

2. Chat-Level Screenshots

For each message thread identified in Item 1, a screenshot of that chat's settings/info screen, showing all information displayed there, including but not limited to:

- whether disappearing messages are enabled (and the timer setting, if so);
- shared media;
- the thread's members/participants; and
- groups in common with other users.

3. Application Settings Screenshots

A screenshot of each of the following settings screens within the Signal application for each employee:

- "Data and Storage"
- "Linked Devices"
- "Backups"
- "Privacy"

4. Home Page Screenshot

A screenshot of the Signal application home page (chat list) for each employee, showing the list of active message threads.

DELIVERY: Please provide records in their original format. For example, email messages in .msg format, including their attachments. Provide text documents on a word-searchable PDF file — capable of Online Text Recognition, and quantitative data in a manipulatable, searchable Excel (XLS) spreadsheet.

As permitted by the CPRA, this Request sets forth the specific categories of information that we are seeking, rather than asking for documents by name [Gov't Code § 7920.530(b)]. It is your obligation to conduct record searches based on the criteria identified herein [see id. §§ 7922.000, 7922.535]. But should you come to believe that the present Request is overly broad, you are required to (1) offer assistance in identifying responsive records and information; (2) describe "the information technology and physical location in which the records exist"; and (3) provide "suggestions for overcoming any practical basis" that you assert as a reason to delay or deny access to the records or information sought [id. § 7922.600(a)].

The CPRA requires that you respond to this Request within ten business days [id. § 7922.535(a)]. No notice shall specify a date that would result in an extension for more than fourteen business days [id. § 7922.535(b)–(c)]. In the written determination, the agency shall state the estimated date when the records will be made available.

If you contend that an express provision of the law exempts a responsive record from disclosure, either in whole or in part, you must make that determination in writing. Such a determination must specify the legal authority on which you rely, as well as identify both the name and title of the person(s) responsible for the determination not to disclose [id. § 7922.000; see also id. § 7922.535(d)].

Additionally, even if you contend that a portion of a record requested is exempt from disclosure, you still must release the non-exempt portion of that record [id. § 7922.525(a), (c)].

Please note that the CPRA "endows" your agency with "discretionary authority to override" any of the Act's statutory exemptions "when a dominating public interest favors disclosure." [CBS, Inc. v. Block, 42 Cal. 3d 646, 652 (1986); see also Nat'l Conference of Black Mayors v. Chico Cmty. Publ'g, Inc., 25 Cal. App. 5th 570, 579 (2018) (construing the CPRA's exemptions as "permissive, not mandatory—they allow nondisclosure but do not prohibit disclosure")]

Because this request pertains to a matter of public concern, I request a fee waiver. None of the information obtained will be sold or distributed for profit. I also request that, to the extent possible, documents be provided in electronic format. Doing so will eliminate the need to copy the materials and provide another basis for the requested fee waiver.

Please copy and send all responsive records as soon as possible, and—if necessary—on a rolling basis to this online records portal. If you have any questions, please email me as soon as possible.

Thank you in advance for your assistance with this request. I look forward to receiving your response within ten business days, by November 30, 2026.

Sincerely,

Robbie Powelson
